cards.name: sink-the-next-global-load-to-the-earliest-legal-seam-in-hand
cards.title: Sink the next global load to the earliest legal seam in hand-edited assembly
cards.description: In hand-edited assembly, hoist a block-head LDS-read burst above the K-guard so the next global load issues a slot earlier: +7.8% on the targeted route
cards.key: rowwise-scaled fp8 (e4m3 fnuz) dense GEMM with a bf16 epilogue, hand-edited phase-2 assembly on gfx942/CDNA3, raw HIP against a vendor-library oracle
cards.effect: +7.8% and +3.75% on the two large-M prefill routes it targeted (M=512,N=11008,K=4096 and M=1024,N=4096,K=11008); 1.1764x final oracle-relative geomean over the 11-case mix, decode cases untouched by these hunks
cards.roofline: latency-bound (issue-slot wait at the head of the loop block) before and after — no bound-class shift; ~0.35 of achievable fp8 MFMA peak vs an oracle at ~0.36 in the same session; minimum traffic puts it far from the memory roof
cards.lever: when a tiled MFMA main loop is issue-bound at the block head, take ownership of the emitted assembly and sink the next K-stage's global-load group to the earliest legal seam: hoist the head LDS-read burst above the K-guard branch so the loads enter the issue queue one guard-evaluation earlier
cards.apply: pure reorder inside one main-loop block per tile shape; de-alias by remapping each load's address temp onto the low pair of that same load's destination quad, so the edit costs zero registers, zero LDS and no occupancy; the assembly becomes the artifact the build installs
cards.stack:
total 1.1764x oracle-relative geomean (director-verified) = the same lever applied to three tile shapes' main loops
- 1. 64x128x128 tile — +3.75% on its declared large-M route (round 3, verified)
- 2. 32x64x256 tile — suite-geomean movement only, null on all four per-route instruments (round 4, verified but unproven; standalone contribution never isolated)
- 3. 128x64x64 tile — +7.8% drift-corrected, n=20 interleaved paired A/B, 20/20 replicates positive (round 5, verified) — the strongest of the three
- note: attribution is incremental in landing order, not independent; per-application effect decayed monotonically (3.75 / 3.00 / 0.91 percent of remaining headroom), the signature of a finite resource
cards.verify: disassemble the code object out of the live shared library and confirm the hunk is actually resident before trusting a timing; then judge on the declared route with a same-session interleaved paired A/B against a zero-signal control route set, and hash the output for bit-exactness
cards.pitfall:
a rebuild scored the same as the incumbent with compile and correctness both green → the edited assembly is not in the build graph and re-entered only through an installed object file, so the timed binary held none of the edit → confirm the hunk in the code object extracted from the live library, not in the source tree
- pitfall: the unchanged tree scored 1.188 and 1.173 within one round → the oracle denominator itself drifts across sessions, so an absolute oracle-relative geomean is uninterpretable alone → interleave A and B in one session and drift-correct against a route set the edit cannot touch
- pitfall: a real +4.4% single-route win was discarded because the 11-case suite geomean moved only ~0.4% → a per-tile-shape edit is diluted about tenfold by a multi-shape mix, below session drift → judge on the route the direction declared and keep the suite geomean as a tripwire
- pitfall: a tolerance-based parity gate passed a reorder that turned a class of NaN into +Inf → a tolerance comparison cannot see a value swap it treats as out-of-range on both sides → gate a pure reorder on a bit-identical output hash instead
cards.caution: also verify where the block's guard already sits: on a tile whose K-guard was already after the head LDS burst the same hoist measured ~0.999 and the register remap was pure cost; also verify that source-level attempts at the same reordering are not being re-scheduled away by the backend before concluding the seam does nothing
cards.source: run team_dense_fp8_gemm_rowwise_20260831_073632_1898252_9464 (2026-08-31); rounds 3/4/5 verifier records and the final director validation
